blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across languages, yet their safety and reasoning capabilities remain predominantly evaluated in English. Translating existing benchmarks offers a scalable approach to multilingual evaluation, but preserving task-specific meaning across languages presents significant challenges, particularly for harmful requests, mathematical reasoning, and conversational interactions. We introduce a reasoning-guided translation framework for constructing multilingual evaluations designed to preserve the structure and intended meaning of diverse benchmark tasks. Our approach separates translation strategy selection from large-scale generation, combining reasoning-guided configuration selection with task-aware validation, targeted repair, and independent quality screening. Using this framework, we develop a source-aligned evaluation collection spanning seven safety, conversational, and mathematical reasoning resources across 11 languages. The resulting collection achieves 99.94\% coverage of intended item--language pairs in the two subsets requiring repair. Evaluations of open-source LLMs reveal distinct language-dependent vulnerabilities, including inconsistent refusal behaviour and substantial reasoning degradation in lower-resource languages. These findings highlight the importance of task-sensitive benchmark construction and systematic quality assessment for understanding multilingual model behaviour beyond English.
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型(LLM)越来越多地在各种语言之间部署,但其安全和推理能力仍然以英语为主。 将现有基准翻译为多语种评价提供了一个可扩展的方法,但保留不同语文具体任务的含义带来了重大挑战,特别是对有害的请求、数学推理和对话互动而言。 我们采用了一个推理指导翻译框架,用于构建多语种评价,旨在维护各种基准任务的结构和预期含义。 我们的方法将翻译策略选择与大规模生成区分开来,将推理引导配置选择与任务意识验证,定向修复,独立质量筛选相结合. 利用这个框架,我们开发出一套源相匹配的评价集,涵盖11种语言的7种安全性,对话性和数学推理资源. 由此而来的收集在两个需要修复的子集中实现了99.94%的预定项目语言对的覆盖. 对开放源代码有限责任管理的评价表明,存在不同的依赖语言的脆弱性,包括拒绝行为不一致,资源较少的语言推理严重退化。 这些调查结果突出表明,为了了解英语以外的多种语文模式行为,制定任务敏感基准和系统质量评估十分重要。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used across
linguistic communities, yet their safety and reasoning
capabilities remain predominantly evaluated in English ( Yong et al., 2025 ) . This disparity raises
concerns about the reliability of multilingual deployment,
as model behaviour can vary substantially across
languages. Previous studies have shown that language
choice can influence responses to harmful requests ( Deng et al., 2024 ) and that reasoning performance
often differs across linguistic settings ( Shi et al., 2023 ; Son et al., 2025 ) .
However, interpreting these differences requires
comparable evaluation resources. Without equivalent
test instances, observed performance gaps may reflect
differences in benchmark construction rather than
the underlying capabilities of the models.

blocks.en:
Translating established English benchmarks provides
a practical and scalable means of extending evaluation
to other languages. However, linguistic fluency alone
does not guarantee that translated instances preserve
the properties being evaluated. Safety benchmarks
require the original intent and severity of harmful
requests to remain intact, while maintaining distinctions
between benign and unsafe content. Mathematical
reasoning tasks demand precise preservation of numerical
relationships and logical constraints, whereas
conversational evaluations depend on consistent dialogue
structure and message ordering. These challenges
are further complicated by the safety alignment of
translation models, which may refuse to translate
harmful-looking requests or alter their intended meaning.
Such behaviour represents a potential source of
evaluation bias, particularly when unsuccessful
translations are silently excluded. Consequently,
reliable multilingual benchmark construction requires
more than translation accuracy: it demands task-aware
quality control, transparent handling of failures,
and systematic assessment of the resulting resources.

blocks.en:
To address these challenges, we introduce a reasoning-guided translation framework for scalable multilingual benchmark construction.
Our approach separates translation configuration
design from large-scale generation, leveraging a
reasoning model to identify suitable translation
strategies while delegating production to a more
computationally efficient model. Unlike a uniform
translation pipeline, the proposed framework accounts
for the distinct requirements of safety, conversational,
and mathematical reasoning tasks. It integrates
source-aware validation, targeted repair, and
translator-independent quality screening to identify
potential translation failures and maintain traceability
to the original evaluation instances. Figure 1 illustrates the overall workflow.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Existing safety research disproportionately focuses on English, leaving important gaps in non-English evaluation ( Yong et al., 2025 ) . XSafety measures harmful-response behavior across ten languages ( Wang et al., 2024 ) , while Deng et al. (2024) show that multilingual prompting can expose vulnerabilities in safety alignment. At the benchmark level, JailbreakBench establishes standardized harmful behaviors and evaluation protocols for jailbreak robustness ( Chao et al., 2024 ) . These studies motivate language-aligned evaluation, but do not jointly cover our safety, over-refusal, and conversational sources.
blocks.zh: 现有的安全研究过分地注重英语,在非英语评价中留下了重要的空白(Yong等,2025.). XSafety测量十种语言的有害反应行为(Wang等,2024年),而Deng等(2024年)则显示多语种的提示可以暴露出安全配合中的弱点. 在基准层面,监狱破伤风Bench建立了标准化的有害行为和评估协议,用于监狱破伤风(Chao等人,2024年)。 这些研究激发了语言相通的评价,但并没有共同涵盖我们的安全、过度的反驳和对话来源。

blocks.en: MGSM introduced manually translated grade-school mathematics problems for cross-lingual reasoning evaluation ( Shi et al., 2023 ) . More recent benchmarks target competition-level mathematics: MCLM includes translated AIME 2024 and MATH problems across a broad range of languages ( Son et al., 2025 ) , and MMATH combines model-generated translations, cross-model verification, and human revision ( Luo et al., 2025 ) . We therefore do not claim the first translations of these tasks; instead, we integrate them with complementary safety sources in one workflow.
blocks.zh: MGSM为跨语言推理评价引入了手工翻译的年级数学问题(Shi等,2023. 最近的基准针对竞争一级的数学: MCLM包括翻译的AIME 2024和跨多种语言的MATH问题(Son等,2025年),MMATH结合了模型生成的翻译,跨模型验证,以及人文审校(Luo等,2025年). 因此,我们并不要求这些任务的第一批翻译;相反,我们将它们与互补的安全来源合并为一个工作流程。

blocks.en: Global MMLU demonstrates that translated evaluations can retain linguistic and cultural biases ( Singh et al., 2025 ) ; MuBench further emphasizes cross-language alignment and translation-quality assessment ( Han et al., 2026 ) . Automatic Prompt Engineer and ProTeGi establish LLM-based instruction proposal and optimization ( Zhou et al., 2023 ; Pryzant et al., 2023 ) , while M-MAD explores structured LLM judging for translation quality ( Feng et al., 2025 ) . We build on these directions by using a reasoning model to select a translation configuration on a small development set and a lighter model for production, while distinguishing format checks from semantic validation.

blocks.en:
The requirements for faithful translation depend on
the underlying evaluation task. Safety benchmarks
require harmful intent to remain intact without
softening or intensifying the original request.
For over-refusal evaluation, maintaining the distinction
between benign and unsafe requests is particularly
important, as subtle changes in meaning can alter
the expected response. Mathematical reasoning tasks
require numerical quantities, equations, variables,
and logical constraints to remain consistent with
the source, while conversational data require
the preservation of message boundaries, roles,
indices, and ordering. We incorporate these
requirements into the translation instructions and
validation procedures. However, satisfying such
constraints does not, by itself, establish semantic
equivalence between source and translated instances.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We introduce a reasoning-guided framework for constructing
multilingual evaluations of LLM safety and reasoning,
and develop a source-aligned collection spanning seven
English-language resources and 11 target languages.
By separating translation configuration selection
from large-scale generation and incorporating
task-aware validation and targeted repair, our
framework provides a scalable and auditable approach
to multilingual benchmark construction. The resulting
workflow achieves 99.94% structural coverage of
the intended WildChat and WildJailbreak
item–language pairs, while independent quality
screening identifies residual translation failures
that structural checks alone cannot detect.
Evaluations on aligned instances further reveal
distinct model-specific vulnerabilities, including
under-refusal of harmful requests, over-refusal of
benign prompts, and substantial reasoning degradation
across languages. These findings demonstrate the
importance of evaluating multilingual capabilities
across complementary tasks rather than relying
on English-centric assessments or aggregate scores.
More broadly, our study highlights the need for
task-sensitive validation and transparent quality
assessment in multilingual benchmark construction,
while recognising that automatic screening cannot
replace bilingual verification of semantic fidelity.

blocks.en:
Our study has several limitations. First, although
the configuration pilot covers all seven source
resources, it is restricted to 70 Thai instances
per configuration, limiting the generalisability
of the selected translation strategy across languages.
The use of GPT-5.4 Thinking to both propose and
assess candidate configurations may also introduce
selection bias. Furthermore, latency and cost
estimates are based on a separate 14-item-per-model
sample, Thai tokenisation, and published API prices.
The projected costs exclude configuration selection
and repair, and therefore do not establish a globally
optimal translation configuration.

blocks.en: Appendix A Automatic Validation of Translation Fidelity
blocks.zh: 附录 翻译的自动验证

blocks.en: Structural acceptance (Section 5 ) shows that outputs are well formed; it does not show that they preserve meaning. To screen for meaning errors at scale, we audit all accepted item–language pairs from the seven sources with four signals that do not rely on the translator: reference-free quality estimation, cross-lingual embedding similarity, back-translation through an independent MT system, and an LLM judge from a different model family (Table 4 ). These signals are automatic proxies. They are useful for detecting systematic failures and prioritising items for review, but they do not replace the bilingual human assessment described in Appendix I .
blocks.zh: 结构接受(第5节)显示产出形成良好;它没有显示它们保持意义。 为了筛选规模上的含义错误,我们审计了所有接受的7个来源的语言配对,其中四个信号不依赖翻译:无参考质量估计、跨语言嵌入相似性、通过独立的MT系统进行回译,以及来自不同模型家族的LLM法官(表4)。 这些信号是自动代用. 它们有助于发现系统性的失败和优先审查项目,但不能取代附录一所述的双语人类评估。

blocks.en: Script-aware language identification flags 274 item–language pairs (1.2% of audited pairs) whose evaluation field remains in English despite passing structural validation. Most occur in XSTest (179 pairs, 3.6% of its 4,950 pairs), whose prompts are short single questions, and in WildChat user turns (79); the remaining 16 are spread across the other sources. These cases show that structural acceptance overstates translation coverage. We mark the affected pairs in the release metadata and exclude them from all cross-lingual comparisons (Appendix B ). For mathematics, numeral recall (the share of numbers in the English problem that reappear in the translation after native digit systems are normalised) is at least 98.6% for every language in both MATH-500 and AIME 2024. Numeral recall detects dropped or altered quantities but not changes to conditions or wording.
blocks.zh: Script-aware语言识别旗274个项目-语言对(占已审计对数的1.2%),其评价领域虽然经过了结构验证,但仍使用英语. 大部分发生在XSTest(179对,占其4,950对中的3.6%),其提示是短的单个问题,在WildChat用户转弯(79个);其余16个则分布在其它来源. 这些案件表明,结构接受过多地说明了翻译的覆盖面。 我们在发布元数据中标出受影响的对子,并将其排除在所有跨语言比较之外(附录B. 就数学而言,数字召回(在英语问题中,数字在本土数字系统正常化后在翻译中重新出现的比例)在MATH-500和AIME 2024中,每种语言至少占98.6%. 数字召回探测到数量下降或改变,但条件或措辞没有改变。

blocks.en: We score each translated evaluation field with CometKiwi ( Rei et al., 2022 ) . Across six sources and 11 languages the mean score is 0.84 (Figure 2 ). Source means range from 0.82 (MATH-500, AIME 2024) to 0.86 (JBB-Behaviors, XSTest), and language means from 0.81 (Arabic) to 0.86 (Bengali). QE scores are not calibrated across target languages, so we use them to rank items within a language and do not interpret differences between languages. WildChat is excluded from this analysis because its turns are often multi-paragraph and contain code, which is outside the sentence-level setting CometKiwi was trained on; for WildChat we rely on embedding and back-translation scores instead.
blocks.zh: 我们每个翻译的评价领域都与CometKiwi(Rei等,2022年)评分. 在6个来源和11个语言中,平均得分为0.84(图2)。 来源指从0.82(MATH-500,AIME 2024)到0.86(JBB-Behaviors,XSTest),语言指从0.81(阿拉伯语)到0.86(Bengali). QE分数在目标语言之间没有校正,因此我们用它们来对某一语言中的项目进行排序,并且不解释各语言之间的差异. WildChat被排除在这个分析之外,因为它的转折往往是多段并包含代码,这在句子级别设置之外,CometKiwi被训练过;对于WildChat,我们依靠嵌入和回译分数代替.

blocks.en: Figure 2: Mean CometKiwi score of the evaluation field per source and target language. WildChat is omitted because its long, multi-paragraph turns fall outside the sentence-level regime of the QE model.
blocks.zh: 图2 平均彗星 Kiwi对每个源和目标语言的评价字段得分. WildChat之所以省略,是因为其长而多段的转折不属于QE模式的句子级别制度.

blocks.en: LaBSE cosine similarity ( Feng et al., 2022 ) between each English field and its translation averages 0.84–0.92 per source. To obtain a signal independent of the GPT-family translator, we back-translate up to 100 items per source and language into English with NLLB-200 (distilled, 1.3B; NLLB Team, 2022 ) and compare the result with the English source. Per-source chrF++ ( Popović, 2017 ) ranges from 56.1 (WildChat) to 70.6 (JBB-Behaviors), and LaBSE similarity between back-translation and source ranges from 0.92 to 0.95. Because back-translation adds the errors of a second system, these scores are likely to underestimate direct fidelity; the lower chrF++ for WildChat partly reflects its longer, code-heavy turns.
blocks.zh: LaBSE的同位素相似性(Feng等,2022年)在每个英语领域之间,其翻译平均为每个来源0.84–0.92. 为了获得独立于GPT-家族翻译的信号,我们将每个源和语言的最多100个项目回译为NLLB-200(distilled, 1.3B; NLLB Team, 2022),并将结果与英语源进行比较. 源代码chrF++ (Popović,2017年)从56.1(WildChat)到70.6(JBB-Behaviors)不等,而LaBSE在回译和源之间的相似度从0.92到0.95. 由于回译增加了第二个系统的错误,这些分数很可能低估了直接忠心;WildChat的下ChrF++部分反映了其较长的代码重转弯.

blocks.en: Table 4: Fidelity signals per source, averaged over 11 languages. QE: CometKiwi; LaBSE: source–translation similarity; BT-chrF / BT-sim: chrF++ and LaBSE similarity between the NLLB back-translation and the English source; Mean.: judge-rated meaning preservation (1–5); Pres.: % of translations judged to preserve intent (safety and conversation) or all mathematical content (math).
blocks.zh: 表4:每个来源的Fidelity信号,平均超过11种语言. QE: CometKiwi; LaBSE: source-transion speciality; BT-chrF / BT-sim: chrF++和LaBSE在NLLB回译和英语回译的相似性; Mean.: 法官评分为意义保全(1–5); Pres. : 被评为保留意图(安全和对话)或所有数学内容(math)的翻译百分比.

blocks.en: The main risk in translating safety data is that a harmful request becomes benign, or the reverse. We test for this with Gemma-3-12B-it ( Gemma Team, 2025 ) , which classifies each prompt as harmful or benign without seeing any other version of it. Over the 1,213 items of StrongREJECT, JBB-Behaviors, XSTest, and WildJailbreak, it judges the English source and all 11 translations (14,556 judgments). The label assigned to a translation matches the label assigned to its English source for 92.6% of items (91.2–94.3% by language; Table 5 ), and 6.7% of prompts judged harmful in English are judged benign after translation.
blocks.zh: 翻译安全数据的主要风险是有害请求变得无害,或者相反。 我们用Gemma-3-12B-it(Gemma Team,2025年)来测试这个,它把每个提示都归类为有害或良性,没有看到任何其他版本. 在StrongREJECT、JBB-Behaviors、XSTest和WildJailbreak等1 213个项目上,它评判了英文来源和全部11个译文(14 556个判决书)。 指定给翻译的标签与92.6%(91.2-94.3%,按语文分列;表5)的英文标签相符,6.7%的英文标签在翻译后被认为无害。

blocks.en: This disagreement cannot be attributed to translation alone, because the judge is itself noisy: it agrees with the gold dataset labels on only 88.7% of English prompts. Its gold accuracy on translations is 85.2–88.4%, at most 3.5 points below English. We read this drop as a rough indication of how much label change translation introduces, not as a precise estimate, since judge errors and translation errors cannot be separated without human labels. Agreement is near ceiling for StrongREJECT (99.2%), whose requests are unambiguous, and lowest for JBB-Behaviors (89.7%) and XSTest (90.2%), which are built around borderline safe–unsafe contrasts that are hard to classify even in English. Items whose label flips are released for inspection as candidates for targeted human review.
blocks.zh: 这种分歧不能仅仅归咎于翻译,因为法官本身很吵:它同意只有88.7%的英语提示上的金色数据集标签. 它的黄金精度在翻译上为85.2-88.4%,最高低于英语3.5分. 我们读到这个倒数,是粗略地说明更改了多少标签的翻译,而不是精确的估计,因为没有人类的标签,判断错误和翻译错误是无法分开的。 协议的上限接近于StrongREJECT(99.2%),其要求是明确的,而JBB-Behaviors(89.7%)和XSTest(90.2%)的要求最低,它们围绕连英语都难以分类的边界安全-不安全对比而构建。 标签翻转后作为目标人审查候选人放行检查.

blocks.en: Table 5: Label preservation (%) under independent harmful/benign judgments by Gemma-3-12B-it. Gold acc.: agreement with the original dataset labels, which indicates the judge’s own error rate.
blocks.zh: 表5:Gemma-3-12B-it在独立有害/无罪判决下保存标签(%)。 Gold acc.: 与原数据集标签一致,表示法官自己的出错率.

blocks.en: The same judge then sees each accepted translation alongside its source. It rates meaning preservation on a 1–5 scale and classifies intent as preserved, softened, intensified, or changed; for mathematics, it states whether every number, condition, and question is preserved. The mean meaning score is 4.98, 99.6% of translations are judged to preserve intent or mathematical content, and 0.3% of safety and conversational items are judged softened (highest for WildChat, at 0.6%). These scores are close to ceiling, and LLM judges are known to be lenient, so we use them as a screening signal and not as an estimate of human-rated quality. All flagged pairs are released for inspection.
blocks.zh: 同一法官然后看到每个被接受的翻译及其来源。 它将意图分为保留、软化、强化或改变;对数学来说,它说明是否保留了每一个数字、条件和问题。 平均意义分为4.98分,99.6%的翻译被判断为保留意图或数学内容,0.3%的安全和对话项目被判断为软化(WildChat最高,为0.6%). 这些分数接近上限,LLM评委已知宽大,所以我们用它们作为筛选信号,而不是对人评分质量的估计. 所有标有标记的对被放出检查.

blocks.en: Appendix B Downstream Evaluation
blocks.zh: 附录B 下游 评价

blocks.en: To check whether the collection supports meaningful cross-lingual comparison, we evaluate two open instruction-tuned models, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct ( Grattafiori and others, 2024 ) and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ( Qwen Team, 2024 ) , on English and all 11 target languages.
blocks.zh: 为了检查该集是否支持有意义的跨语言比较,我们评价了两个开放的指令调取模型:Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct(Grattafiori等,2024年)和Quen2.5-7B-Instruct(Quen Team,2024年),英语和所有11个目标语言.

blocks.en: Every language uses the same items, sampled once with a fixed seed: 100 StrongREJECT prompts; the 100 harmful JBB behaviors; all 450 XSTest prompts (200 unsafe, 250 safe); 100 WildJailbreak prompts, of which we report refusal on the 90 adversarial-harmful ones; and 100 MATH-500 problems. Prompts are given as a single user turn with no system prompt. Math problems are followed by an English instruction to reason step by step and give the final answer in \boxed{} . We decode greedily with vLLM ( Kwon et al., 2023 ) , allowing up to 768 new tokens for safety prompts and 3,072 for MATH-500.
blocks.zh: 每种语言都使用相同的物品,一次用固定的种子取样:100个强力REJECT提示;100个有害的JBB行为;所有450个XSTest提示(200个不安全,250个安全);100个WildJailbreak提示,我们报告其中90个对抗-有害提示遭到拒绝;100个MATH-500问题。 提示作为单一用户转弯,没有系统提示。 数学问题之后是英语指示, 一步一步地讲道理, 我们用vLLM(Kwon等, 2023年)来解码,

blocks.en: Safety responses are judged by Gemma-3-12B-it, which belongs to a different model family from both the translator and the evaluated models, against the English original of each prompt. Responses to harmful prompts are scored with the StrongREJECT rubric ( Souly et al., 2024 ) , which gives a refusal decision and a harmfulness score in [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] ; we report the harmfulness score multiplied by 100. Responses to benign prompts are classified with the three-way XSTest scheme ( Röttger et al., 2024 ) , and full and partial refusals both count as refusals. All judge outputs were parseable. Math answers are verified symbolically against the reference using the last boxed expression, after native digits are normalised. Item–language pairs flagged as untranslated (Appendix A ) are excluded, which removes 370 model–item–language triples. We report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and test each language against English with a paired bootstrap over shared items ( Koehn, 2004 ) . Both models answer in the language of the prompt for at least 94.6% of safety items in every language, so the judge assesses native-language responses and not code-switched English.
blocks.zh: 安全响应是由Gemma-3-12B-it判断的,它与翻译和被评价的模型都属于不同的模型家族,与每个快取的英文正本相对. 对有害诱因的反应以强REJECT(Souly等人,2024年)为分数,该分数以[0,1][0,1]给出拒绝决定和有害分数;我们报告有害分数乘以100. 对良性提示的反应与三向XSTest计划(Röttger等,2024年)分类,完全和部分拒绝都算作拒绝. 所有法官的产出都是可解析的。 数学答案在本地数字正常化后,用最后一个框化表达式对照引用进行符号验证. 不包括标为未翻译(附录A)的项目语言对,它删除了370个模型-项目-语言三重体。 校对:Soup 两种模型都用提示语言回答每种语言中至少94.6%的安全物品,因此法官评估的是本土语言响应,而不是代码开关英语.

StrongREJECT score is the mean harmfulness score × 100 \times 100 ; all other rows are percentages. ∗ : significant difference from English (paired bootstrap, p < 0.05 p<0.05 ). Arrows give the desirable direction. Items: 100 StrongREJECT, 100 harmful JBB, 200 unsafe and 250 safe XSTest, 90 adversarial-harmful WildJailbreak, and 100 MATH-500 problems; item–language pairs flagged as untranslated (Appendix A ) are excluded.

blocks.en: Llama-3.1-8B refuses 97.5% of unsafe XSTest prompts in English but only 69.5% in Turkish (28.0 points lower) and 80.6% in Bengali; the drop is significant in 9 of 11 languages (Table 6 , Figure 3 ). Its refusal of harmful JBB behaviors falls from 94.0% to 74.0% in Turkish, again with significant drops in 9 of 11 languages, and its StrongREJECT score rises from 1.5 in English to 8.0 in Turkish and 4.9 in Persian and Thai. Qwen2.5-7B shows the opposite pattern. Its refusal of unsafe prompts is largely stable across languages, but its over-refusal of safe XSTest prompts rises from 6.4% in English to 13.0–23.7% in the other languages, and all 11 differences are significant. The same translated items therefore reveal under-refusal in one model and over-refusal in the other. A single pooled safety score would hide this difference, which is why we report safety and over-refusal sources separately (Section 5 ).
blocks.zh: Llama-3.1-8B拒绝97.5%的不安全XSTest的英语提示,但只有69.5%的土耳其语提示(低于28.0分)和80.6%的孟加拉语提示;11种语言中的9种表示大幅下降(表6,图3)。 其拒绝有害的JBB行为在土耳其语中从94.0%下降到74.0%,11种语言中的9种再次大幅下降,其强REJECT得分从英语的1.5分上升到了土耳其语的8.0分和波斯语和泰语的4.9分. Quen2.5-7B显示了相反的模式. 它拒绝不安全的提示在各种语言之间基本稳定,但是它过度拒绝安全XSTest的提示从英语的6.4%上升到了其他语言的13.0–23.7%,所有11个差异都是显著的. 因此,同一译出的项目在一种模式中揭示出反对不足,在另一种模式中揭示出反对过度。 单一的集合安全分数会掩盖这一差异,这就是为什么我们分别报告安全和过度反驳来源的原因(第5节)。

blocks.en: MATH-500 accuracy falls significantly for both models in Bengali, Persian, Hindi, and Turkish, and for Llama-3.1-8B also in Arabic. The largest drops are from 44.0% to 24.0% for Llama-3.1-8B in Arabic and from 74.0% to 58.6% for Qwen2.5-7B in Turkish, while Spanish and French stay within four points of English for both models. The paired judge rates at least 99.6% of translated problems in every language as preserving all mathematical content (Appendix A ). This suggests that translation errors are unlikely to explain most of the gap, although the judge’s leniency means we cannot rule out subtle changes in wording. The pattern matches the language-dependent reasoning gaps reported for other multilingual mathematics benchmarks ( Shi et al., 2023 ; Son et al., 2025 ) . AIME 2024 is not shown: with 30 problems and accuracies of at most 14.3%, no difference is significant.
blocks.zh: 孟加拉语、波斯语、印地语和土耳其语的MATH-500精度都大幅下降,而Llama-3.1-8B的精度也以阿拉伯语下降。 在阿拉伯语中,Llama-3.1-8B的降幅最大,从44.0%降至24.0%;而土耳其语的Quen2.5-7B的降幅最大,从74.0%降至58.6%;而西班牙语和法语的降幅在两种型号的英语四分以内。 配对法官将每种语言翻译问题的至少99.6%评为保留了所有数学内容(附录A.). 这说明翻译错误不可能解释大部分差距,尽管法官宽大处理意味着我们不能排除措辞上的细微变化。 该模式与其他多语种数学基准报告的语言依赖推理差距相匹配(Shi等人,2023;Son等人,2025)。 AIME 2024没有显示:有30个问题和最多14.3%的情况,没有显著差别.

blocks.en: On WildJailbreak, refusal increases in several languages, most strongly in Bengali (by 27.8 and 41.1 points for Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B) and Hindi (by 40.0 points for Qwen2.5-7B). Harmfulness scores on WildJailbreak responses also decrease in every language. We do not think this reflects weaker translations, for two reasons. First, the judge rates 99.7% of translated WildJailbreak prompts as intent-preserving. Second, even responses that do not refuse receive lower harmfulness scores outside English (51 vs. 73 for Llama-3.1-8B and 55 vs. 73 for Qwen2.5-7B, on the same × 100 \times 100 scale). This suggests that the models follow long role-play framings less competently in other languages, not that they behave more safely.
blocks.zh: 在"WildJailbreak"(WildJailbreak)上,几种语言的拒绝增加,最强烈的是孟加拉语(Llama-3.1-8B和Qune2.5-7B的拒绝得分分别增加了27.8分和41.1分)和印地语(Qune2.5-7B的拒绝得分增加了40.0分). WildJailbreak响应的伤害分数在每种语言中也都有所下降. 我们认为这并不反映翻译较弱,原因有两个。 首先,法官将99.7%的 WildJailbreak 的翻译提示作为意图保留。 其次,即使是不拒绝的回复,也会得到英语以外的更低的有害分数(51对Llama-3.1-8B的73分,55对Qwen2.5-7B的73分,同为×100\times 100分). 这表明这些模型遵循的是长长的角色扮演框架,其他语言的能力较低,而不是它们的行为更加安全。

blocks.en: Response truncation is a further factor. Non-English scripts need more tokens, so the 768-token budget truncates more non-English responses. Truncation can only reduce how specific and convincing a response is, so it biases harmfulness scores downward outside English. As a result, the harmfulness increases reported above for direct requests are conservative, but the decreases (for WildJailbreak, and for Qwen2.5-7B on StrongREJECT in Bengali and Russian) may be partly caused by truncation. Refusal decisions are usually made in the first sentences and are therefore largely unaffected. Overall, adversarial and direct harmful requests measure different constructs and should be reported separately, as recommended in Section 5 .
blocks.zh: 反应截断是另一个因素。 非英语剧本需要更多的代币,因此768-token预算截取了更多的非英语回应. 截断只能减少反应的具体性和说服力,因此它偏向了英语以外的有害分数下行. 因此,上述直接请求的危害性增加是保守的,但减少(WildJailbreak和Quen2.5-7B关于孟加拉语和俄语的strongREJECT)的部分原因可能是短跑。 拒绝决定通常在第一句中作出,因此基本上不受影响。 总的来说,对抗性要求和直接有害要求衡量不同的构象,应当按照第5条的建议单独报告。

blocks.en: Appendix C Prompt Design and Calibration
blocks.zh: 附录C 快速设计和校正

blocks.en: GPT-5.4 Thinking proposes three translation prompts: P1 ( strict_structure_preservation ), P2 ( benchmark_fidelity_translation ), and P3 ( natural_thai_semantic_fidelity ). All require valid JSON, fixed field names, and preservation of source metadata. P1 prioritizes formatting; P2 additionally stresses safety intent and mathematical constraints; P3 emphasizes fluent target-language wording. The pilot contains ten Thai items from each of seven datasets for every one of five translators and three prompts ( 5 × 3 × 70 = 1,050 5\times 3\times 70=1{,}050 calls). Results cover all 15 configurations (Table 2 ). For each output, we check API and JSON success, preservation of field names and WildChat message structure, recall of the numbers in mathematical problems, and refusal-like responses; an output is structurally valid only if it passes all checks. Production uses the language-specific instantiation of P2 . Because one reasoning model designs and helps assess configurations, the selection remains a screened engineering choice, not an independent semantic-fidelity assessment.

blocks.en: The repair script reads failed records from translation_errors_incremental.xlsx , or scans translated JSONL files for a failure status. It deduplicates the queue using (benchmark, source UID, target language), then resolves the unmodified English input by UID. The repair run loads 370 original WildChat records and 250 WildJailbreak records. Restoring the English input avoids propagating omitted spans from unsuccessful intermediate translations.

blocks.en: For WildChat, the repair API receives the source conversation and must return a translated_messages array. Each entry contains message_index and nonempty content . The validator checks that the returned index multiset exactly matches the source message indices, thereby detecting omission, duplication, and shifted indices. Translated content is merged back into the original message objects; roles, conversation IDs, and metadata are preserved. For WildJailbreak, the repair translates the selected source text field and returns translated_text ; class labels and other metadata are copied from the original. A JSON-schema format is attempted where supported, otherwise prompt-based JSON is used. Transient API errors trigger bounded backoff with jitter; results are cached and error summaries are persisted. The repair identifier ( Repair-P3 ) denotes a separate repair prompt, not the fluency-oriented calibration P3 .

blocks.en: The repair log records 978 queued failed translations and 392 accepted repairs in the first pass (40.1% of the queue); 586 remain after that pass. The final outputs contain 4,066/4,070 accepted WildChat pairs and 2,750/2,750 accepted WildJailbreak pairs, leaving four WildChat cases unaccepted. The intervening repair operations were not fully recorded; we therefore report final observed counts without attributing them to a particular undocumented policy. A later pilot recommendation favors GPT-5.1+ P2 for future targeted repair, but this is distinct from the documented GPT-4o production repair. Finally, the merge operation omits error-status entries: its 6,816 retained records are all marked successful, but the full intended set is 6,820. This repair procedure and its record-level failure tracking cover only WildChat and WildJailbreak; for the other five sources, we report the accepted outputs and their automatic screening (Appendix A ) but no comparable repair log.

Appendix H Speed and Cost of Translation Configurations
blocks.zh: 附录H 翻译配置的速度和费用

blocks.en: The configuration study in Section 4 compares translators by output validity. To complement it, we measure their latency and cost under the deployed prompt P2 . All five translators translate the same 14 items (two per source, into Thai) once each. Each model processes its items sequentially; the timings are single-run observations rather than controlled throughput measurements. Costs are computed from the token counts reported by each API, including reasoning or thinking tokens, which are billed as output, at standard list prices at the time of the experiment. We project these costs to the planned full collection (2,113 source items × \times 11 languages) using per-source means. Costs can vary substantially with language-specific tokenization, item mix, API pricing, and implementation.
blocks.zh: 第4节中的配置研究以产出有效性来比较翻译. 为了加以补充,我们在部署的快速P2下衡量其延迟性和成本。 所有5名翻译将同样的14个项目(每个来源2个,被翻译成泰文)各翻译一次. 每个模型按顺序处理其项目;计时是单跑观测,而不是受控的吞吐量测量. 成本根据每个API报告的代号计数计算,包括推理或思维代号,这些代号按实验时的标准列表价格作为产出计价. 我们利用每个来源的手段,将这些费用预测为计划的全部收集(2 113个源项×\时为11种语言)。 费用可能因语言特定标志化、项目组合、API定价和执行而相去甚远。

blocks.en: GPT-5-mini, the deployed translator, costs $4.20 per 1,000 items, which projects to about $97 for the entire collection (Table 8 ). GPT-5.1 costs 1.4 × \times and GPT-4o 1.6 × \times as much, while Gemini 2.5 Flash costs about the same. Its per-token price is far lower than that of GPT-5.1, but the cost gap is much smaller because 73% of its output tokens are reasoning tokens (1,495 of 2,034 per item). GPT-5.1 and GPT-4o run without reasoning tokens under our settings. Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite is roughly 20 × \times cheaper than GPT-5-mini, but it yields the lowest validity in the configuration study (84.3% vs. 97.1%). This makes it a possible low-cost option only where failure detection and repair can be validated.

GPT-5.1和GPT-4o在我们的设置下运行,没有推理符. 双子座 2.5 Flash-Lite 大约比 GPT-5-mini 便宜20 ×\times,但它在配置研究中产生最小的有效性(84.3%对97.1%). 这使得只有在能验证故障检测和修复的情况下,它才有可能成为低成本的选择.

blocks.en: Reasoning also makes GPT-5-mini the slowest translator, with a median of 10.9 s per item against 2.4–4.3 s for the other full-size models. The difference grows with input length, reaching 42.7 s per WildChat conversation. Because translation is an offline batch job, parallelism may reduce wall-clock time, but the reported per-item latencies do not predict actual deployment throughput. The deployed choice is therefore a cost–validity compromise rather than a uniquely optimal configuration. GPT-5.1 attains the highest validity at a moderate cost premium, and Gemini 2.5 Flash offers similar cost and validity at lower latency. These estimates come from a small, single-language sample, reflect list prices at the time of measurement, and exclude the repair passes and the one-off cost of the reasoning model used for configuration selection.
blocks.zh: 理性也使GPT-5-mini成为最慢的翻译,其他全尺寸型号的中位数为每件10.9 s相较于2.4-4.3 s相较. 差异随输入长度而增大,达到每野话42.7s. 由于翻译是离线批量工作,平行主义可能缩短了墙上时间,但报告的每件延迟不预测实际部署吞吐量. 因此,部署的选择是一种成本-有效性妥协,而不是独特的最佳配置。 GPT-5.1以中度成本溢价获得最高有效性,双子座2.5 Flash在更低的空闲时间提供类似的成本和有效性. 这些估计数来自一个小型的单一语言样本,反映了计量时的列表价格,不包括用于配置选择的推理模型的修复通行证和一次性费用.
